scope: Design-only independent review; project edits, remote calls, commits, inference and Test evaluation are zero.
problem: On the fixed Cap MLP16 quantity-only model, compare the existing log-space squared loss against literal quantity-unit squared and absolute losses, without conflating the result with a backbone change.

new_objectives.raw_mse: mean((existing_predicted_quantity - capped_target_quantity)^2) over the same valid targets
new_objectives.raw_mae: mean(abs(existing_predicted_quantity - capped_target_quantity)) over the same valid targets

material_options.benefit: Directly compares the requested quantity-unit objectives and retains a simple, auditable definition.
material_options.tradeoff: Magnitude, outlier emphasis, gradient norms and clipping frequency change together. Fixed learning rate does not equate effective update sizes or optimization difficulty.
material_options.implementation_cost: Small objective branch plus strict identity/gradient/state and synthetic full-flow checks; reuse training and queue.

material_options.option: Scale-normalized raw objectives or tuned per-loss learning rate
material_options.tradeoff: Changes the approved literal-objective comparison and introduces additional design choices or tuning; would require a distinct later experiment.
material_options.implementation_cost: Additional scale contract/control arms and validation budget; do not add now.

required_implementation_checks.check: Use the canonical existing differentiable point prediction in quantity units and the same Cap target/mask. Here raw means original quantity units of the Cap dataset, not uncapped target data. Do not introduce new output clipping, cap clipping, inverse-link formula, normalization, target reconstruction or changed dtype/precision policy.

Match the existing target population and reduction: same valid events, same per-batch mean and dataset-weighted telemetry. MSE has no square root and no one-half coefficient; MAE has no smoothing or Huber transition. At zero residual, preserve the pinned framework absolute-value subgradient convention.

joint must be the chosen quantity loss tensor itself, not quantity plus zero times TimeNLL. Every optimizer update must preserve time-exclusive grad=None, absent AdamW state and exact time-head tensor values. Shared weights and time inputs remain learnable through quantity.

Bind raw_mse/raw_mae identity consistently into jobs, histories, selected/terminal checkpoints, train and Validation receipts, and replay verification. Existing head family name may be inherited, but objective metadata must not falsely label the optimized loss as log-MSE. Report the unchanged log loss only as an auxiliary metric if retained.

All model tensors, construction/RNG consumption, data order, head initialization, AdamW settings, clip threshold and budget remain identical across new losses and the fixed log-loss reference. No baseline warm start, retry or retraining.

Literal raw MSE can produce larger gradients and objective values. Preserve nonfinite values/errors explicitly; do not silently normalize, clip predictions/residuals or alter optimization to rescue an arm. Keep unused TimeNLL diagnostic failures distinct from quantity-objective failures.

All arms including MAE training select the first strict finite minimum full-Validation quantity RMSE. Read MAE and TimeNLL from that same checkpoint. This tests each objective under the common RMSE selector, not each arm individually optimized for its preferred reporting metric.

Use the stored completed alpha0 log-loss9 references only, SHA-bound to selected checkpoints and native Validation. The same dataset/seed stays on its previous host; new18 split8 on5080 and10 on5090, with at most3 new workers each.

Keep the inherited absolute host deadline and existing per-fit limits. Start only after the prior queues on that host have verified completion and owned PID/GPU absence; allow only the exact still-paused external process identities. No old signals, claim deletion, runtime mutation or source947 changes.

Compare27 endpoints (stored9 plus new18), same target/host/cohorts and3seed mean/sampleSD. Include every seed and worsening case; overall,cap-hit and empty above-cap tail remain distinct. No dataset pooling or best-Test selection.

scientific_interpretation: This is an objective-function comparison with a fixed backbone; it cannot establish a backbone contribution.

Changing log-MSE to raw MSE/MAE jointly changes prediction-scale emphasis, gradient magnitude, curvature/subgradient behavior, clipping and AdamW trajectories. Improvement is not proof that input log1p was wrong or that curvature alone caused earlier errors.

Raw MSE aligns the training target error units with quantity RMSE, while raw MAE aligns with quantity MAE; neither guarantees lower validation error under finite data, a constrained model, optimization and the shared RMSE checkpoint selector.
Raw MAE is less sensitive to the magnitude of an individual residual than MSE, but cannot be claimed to improve both RMSE and MAE or every quantity cohort in advance.

TimeNLL remains a diagnostic of the time-loss-untrained head. Its values must not be discarded or mistaken for a trained time forecast; shared representations may change despite unchanged time-head tensors.
The results remain Cap-data Validation comparisons. They do not demonstrate performance on uncapped quantities or new Test generalization.
next_step: Review only the newly prepared worker/runtime/manager/comparator and run their focused synthetic tests after implementation freezes. No design blocker requires a new user permission question.
